title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
authors: N. Shazeer, A. Mirhoseini, K. Maziarz, A. Davis, Q. Le, G. Hinton, J. Dean
before: Model capacity and compute per example rose together, so bigger meant slower.
problem: You cannot afford to run every parameter on every token.
breakthrough: Thousands of expert subnetworks with a gate selecting a few per token, adding capacity without adding compute.
why: It revived the 1991 mixture-of-experts idea at scale and set up GShard, Switch, Mixtral and the DeepSeek line.
next: GShard and Switch Transformer industrialised the routing.
inherits: Sparse activation, now standard in frontier models.
